title: The day's numbers with a meal whose protein nobody knows
seen: On 1 Nov a restaurant meal was logged with kcal only. The reply showed 48.4 g protein and said 'you need at least ~102 g more', which is misleading: the meal's protein was unknown. On 31 Oct the built-in sum said 256 over rows summing to 2,369 and the model summed by hand.

ledger_rows: restaurant steak + garlic mash + mushroom sauce

turns: So what are we at for today?
facts: The owner's targets are {target_kcal} kcal and a protein floor of {target_protein} g per day.

Today's food ledger: drink 66 kcal / 3.3 g, breakfast 196 / 17.5, lunch 517 / 27.1, drink2 90 / 0.5, lunch2 923 kcal with NO protein figure. The day's total is exactly 1792 kcal, and the protein known so far is 48.4 g from four rows; the fifth row's protein is unknown.
Left against the target: 608 kcal. Protein left is at most 106.6 g against the floor of {target_protein} g, less whatever the restaurant meal held.

criteria.text: The reply gives today's total as 1,792 kcal (or 1792). Any other total fails.

The reply makes clear that the protein figure is only partly known: it gives 48.4 g (or about 48 g) as what is known AND says one meal or row has no protein figure, so the real protein is higher or unknown.

The reply does not tell the owner they firmly 'need' a particular number of grams of protein more as if it were exact. Saying 'at most', 'up to', 'less whatever that meal held' or that the remaining protein is unknown passes; 'you need at least ~102 g more' fails.
The delivered reply has no line starting '(Correction:'.
